# The Jesus Archive

> A free, ad-free reading room of every surviving witness to Jesus of Nazareth, each in its own words with sources: the Old Testament prophecies and the New Testament, Roman and Jewish writers (Tacitus, Josephus, Pliny, Suetonius, the Talmud), the early Church Fathers, archaeology (the Pilate stone, the Caiaphas ossuary, the Isaiah scroll), the other gospels, and the manuscript record.

## About
- [About The Jesus Archive](https://thejesusarchive.com/about): Who edits The Jesus Archive, how its sources are chosen and cited, and how to report an error. An independent, free archive with no ads or login.
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://thejesusarchive.com/faq): Short, sourced answers to common questions about the historical Jesus: did he exist, what Roman and Jewish writers said, the Gospels, the manuscripts…

## Studies
- [Prophecy and Fulfilment](https://thejesusarchive.com/prophecies): Thirty-six passages from Israel’s scriptures set beside the New Testament scenes that read them as fulfilled in Jesus, from Bethlehem to the right hand of God.
- [The Resurrection](https://thejesusarchive.com/resurrection): Eight lines of evidence, drawn from the Gospels, Paul, Roman and Jewish writers and the first Christian leaders, set side by side for the reader to weigh.
- [How the Text Survived](https://thejesusarchive.com/manuscripts): No original of any New Testament book survives, but thousands of copies do, some within decades or a few generations of the writing, more than for any other…
- [The Life of Christ](https://thejesusarchive.com/life): The life of Jesus told in order, from the angel’s message in Nazareth to the empty tomb and Pentecost, each scene linked to the Gospels that tell it.
- [The Timeline](https://thejesusarchive.com/timeline): Every witness in this archive, placed in the order it was written or made: prophecy and Gospel, historian and Father, stone and scroll.
- [Start Here: Twelve Stops Through the Evidence](https://thejesusarchive.com/path): Twelve stops through the oldest evidence for Jesus of Nazareth, beginning with the earliest, written by those closest to him, and moving outward to Roman…

- [Piedras y rollos](https://thejesusarchive.com/es/archaeology): Inscripciones, osarios, mosaicos y rollos: huellas que se pueden tocar del mundo en que vivió Jesús y de los primeros que lo adoraron.

- [Numbers: the bronze serpent and the star](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/numbers): The fourth book of the Torah, following Israel through the wilderness. Chapter 21 tells of the bronze serpent lifted on a pole, and chapter 24 of Balaam’s…
- [2 Samuel: the promise to David](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/2-samuel): The story of David’s reign, c. 1000 BC. In chapter 7 God promises David, through the prophet Nathan, a son and a throne established forever, the root of…
- [Psalms: the songs read of the Messiah](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/psalms): Eight of Israel’s psalms that the New Testament reads as speaking of Jesus: royal songs of the king God enthrones, and laments of a righteous sufferer…
- [Isaiah: the chapters read as prophecy](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/isaiah): The longest of the prophets, from Jerusalem in the eighth century BC. These chapters, from the sign of Immanuel to the suffering servant of chapter 53, are…
- [Jeremiah: Rachel’s weeping and the new covenant](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/jeremiah): The prophet of Jerusalem’s last years before the Babylonian conquest. Chapter 31 holds Rachel weeping for her children and the promise of a new covenant…
- [Daniel: the vision of the Son of Man](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/daniel): Visions of the empires and of God’s coming kingdom. In chapter 7 one like a son of man comes with the clouds to receive an everlasting dominion, the figure…
- [Hosea: out of Egypt I called my son](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/hosea): A prophet of the northern kingdom in the eighth century BC. Chapter 11 remembers God calling Israel, his son, out of Egypt, a line Matthew applies to the…
- [Joel: the Spirit poured out](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/joel): A prophet of the day of Yahweh. Chapter 2 promises that God will pour out his Spirit on all flesh, the passage Peter quoted at Pentecost.
- [Jonah: three days in the fish](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/jonah): The story of a prophet who flees God’s call and is swallowed by a great fish for three days and three nights, the sign Jesus gave of his own death and rising.
- [Micah: the ruler from Bethlehem](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/micah): A prophet of Judah in the late eighth century BC. Chapter 5 looks for a ruler of Israel from Bethlehem, David’s town, whose origins are from of old.
- [Zechariah: the humble king and the stricken shepherd](https://thejesusarchive.com/scripture/old-testament/zechariah): A prophet of the return from exile. These chapters, of the king riding on a donkey, the thirty pieces of silver, the one who was pierced and the shepherd…
